why: Changing O1 to prefer markers that end a self-contained assertion pushed the scorer to pick later, assertion-ending cuts and avoid earlier intra-clause cuts; that shift improved cohesion for longer-latency bins (≤10 and overall) but degraded short-latency bins (≤3 and ≤5). Rank_depth drops at the top positions show the edit changed the model's early choices (so it could and did hurt short-budget behavior), and the tails illustrate this trade — e.g. better grouping of names/enumerations but worse attachment/splitting of dependent clauses like the 'Symptoms, such as vomiting...' example.
lesson: Do not globally prefer later assertion-ending markers at the cost of removing earlier intra-clause cut candidates needed by short-latency budgets; preserve early cut options (or scope the preference) so short-depth rankings are not degraded.
